title: Hardship and Protective Holds — Ending Terms by Tier
content:
The terms on which a hold of **Hardship and Protective Holds** may end early, how long certain holds continue after a qualifying event, when the consumer is told the hold is ending and how long after it ends outbound collection contact may resume, are fixed per tier as follows.

## Ending terms

| Tier | Consumer may end the hold early at any time | Hold ended when its documentation is found invalid | Days after the client's assistance decision on which the hold ends | Days the hold continues after active duty ends | End-of-hold notice (calendar days before the current end date) | Delay before outbound contact resumes (calendar days after the hold ends) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 30-Day Hardship Pause | Yes | Yes | 0 | 0 | 5 | 3 |
| Documented Hardship Hold | Yes | Yes | 0 | 0 | 10 | 7 |
| Disaster Relief Hold | Yes | Yes | 0 | 0 | 10 | 14 |
| Financial Assistance Review Hold | Yes | Yes | 30 | 0 | 10 | 14 |
| Long-Term Hardship Hold | Yes | Yes | 0 | 0 | 15 | 14 |
| Military Service Hold | Yes | Yes | 0 | 90 | 15 | 30 |

## Terms explained

- **Consumer may end the hold early** — whether the consumer may end the hold early at any time.
- **Hold ended when documentation is found invalid** — whether a hold is ended when its documentation is found invalid.
- **Days after the client's assistance decision** — the calendar days after the client's financial assistance decision on which the hold ends; 0 where the tier is not a financial assistance tier.
- **Days the hold continues after active duty ends** — the calendar days the hold continues after active duty ends; 0 where the tier is not a military tier.
- **End-of-hold notice** — the calendar days before the hold's current end date on which the end-of-hold notice is sent.
- **Delay before outbound contact resumes** — the calendar days after the hold ends before outbound collection contact resumes.

## Points of reading

- Every tier lets the consumer end the hold early at any time, and every tier ends a hold whose documentation is found invalid.
- Only the Financial Assistance Review Hold carries a figure for the client's assistance decision (30 days), and only the Military Service Hold carries a post-service figure (90 days).
- The Military Service Hold has the longest delay before outbound contact resumes, 30 calendar days.

## Illustration (hypothetical)

A Long-Term Hardship Hold has a current end date of 20 November. Its end-of-hold notice is sent 15 calendar days before that date, on 5 November; after the hold ends, outbound collection contact resumes no sooner than 14 calendar days later.
